title: BCCDC-PHL/threshold pipeline parameters
description: QC and routine analysis for microbial genomics

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to comma-separated file containing information about the samples in the experiment.
input.help_text: You will need to create a design file with information about the samples in your experiment before running the pipeline. Use this parameter to specify its location. It has to be a comma-separated file with 3 columns, and a header row.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

max_samples.description: Limit the number of samples run by pipeline

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_group_by.description: Also write a MultiQC report and sample_summary.csv per value of these samplesheet fields, under groups/<field>/<value>/.
multiqc_group_by.help_text: Comma-separated list of project_id, tags, sample_type and/or platform. Each tag in a sample's colon-separated tags is its own group. Samples with no value for a field are in no group for it. The all-samples report and sample_summary.csv are always written. Set to an empty string to turn per-group reports off.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

task_tmpdir.description: Give each task a TMPDIR inside its own work directory.
task_tmpdir.help_text: Nextflow forwards the host TMPDIR into Apptainer/Singularity containers but only mounts the task work directory, so a host TMPDIR elsewhere (e.g. under $HOME) is missing inside the container and tools writing temporary files fail. With this on, each task uses a tmp/ directory inside its work directory, which is always mounted and cleaned up with it. Set to false to keep the host TMPDIR.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).

dehosting_options.title: Dehosting options
dehosting_options.description: Options for removing host (e.g. human) reads early in the pipeline.

skip_dehosting.description: Skip the host read removal step.

dehost_reference.description: Host reference genome as FASTA (optionally gzipped) or a prebuilt minimap2 .mmi index. Required unless --skip_dehosting is set.
dehost_reference.help_text: For real runs, point this at a masked human reference (e.g. the masked T2T-CHM13+HLA reference distributed with hostile). Pin the reference version for reproducibility.

publish_dehosted_reads.description: Also publish the final (dehosted) reads to dehost/. Off by default; can also be turned on per sample with the samplesheet's publish_dehosted_reads column.
publish_dehosted_reads.help_text: Trimmed reads from before dehosting still contain host reads and are never published while dehosting runs. With --skip_dehosting the trimmed reads are the final reads, so this option publishes those instead (to fastp/ or fastplong/).

dehost_scrub_headers.description: Replace read headers with anonymised indices in the dehosted reads (off by default to preserve provenance).

species_id_options.title: Species ID, reference and assembly options
species_id_options.description: Species identification (sylph) checked against the samplesheet's expected_taxid, per-isolate reference genome, and draft assembly of isolates.

skip_species_id.description: Skip species identification (sylph) and the check against the samplesheet's expected_taxid.

sylph_db.description: Default sylph genome database (.syldb) of reference genomes to compare reads against. Required unless --skip_species_id is set, or every sample's project lists its own databases in --project_sylph_dbs.

project_sylph_dbs.description: Optional CSV of project_id,sylph_db (one-to-many): the sylph databases each project's samples are screened against, only these, unless the reserved value 'default' is listed.
project_sylph_dbs.help_text: A project listed in this file is screened ONLY against the databases listed for it, not --sylph_db; use the reserved value 'default' as a sylph_db to include --sylph_db as well. Samples whose project isn't listed (or that have none) use --sylph_db. All of a sample's databases are profiled in one sylph call, so the result is a single combined profile. Relative paths are resolved from the directory you launch the pipeline in.

kraken2_db.description: Default kraken2 database directory (the one holding hash.k2d). Optional: kraken2 only runs for samples that have a kraken2 database, this one or their project's in --project_kraken2_dbs.

project_kraken2_dbs.description: Optional CSV of project_id,kraken2_db (one-to-many): the kraken2 databases each project's samples are screened against, only these unless the reserved value 'default' is listed.
project_kraken2_dbs.help_text: A project listed in this file is screened ONLY against the databases listed for it, not --kraken2_db; use the reserved value 'default' as a kraken2_db to include --kraken2_db as well. Samples whose project isn't listed (or that have none) use --kraken2_db. Unlike sylph, kraken2 runs once per database, and the species check keeps the best verdict (a viral sample is expected to be unclassified in a bacterial database). Relative paths are resolved from the directory you launch the pipeline in.

kraken2_min_expected_pct.description: kraken2 species check: minimum % of the classified reads that must be in the expected taxa for a match.
kraken2_min_expected_pct.help_text: Applies to samples that aren't metagenomic. The expected taxa can be at any rank (e.g. a family); reads in nested expected taxa are counted once.

kraken2_min_classified_pct.description: kraken2 species check: below this % of all reads classified, no match/mismatch call is made (verdict low_classified).
kraken2_min_classified_pct.help_text: If most reads are unclassified, the classified ones say little about the sample, so the check reports low_classified rather than a match or mismatch. Not applied to metagenomic samples, where much is expected to be unknown.

kraken2_min_metagenomic_pct.description: kraken2 species check, metagenomic samples: minimum % of the classified reads that must be in the expected taxa.
kraken2_min_metagenomic_pct.help_text: For metagenomic samples an expected taxon only needs to be present, not dominant.

project_expected_taxids.description: Optional CSV of project_id,expected_taxid (one-to-many): expected taxa for samples that don't have their own expected_taxid.
project_expected_taxids.help_text: A project can be listed several times. A sample is checked against its project's taxids when it has no expected_taxid of its own; it matches if its species-ID hit is within any of them, at any rank (e.g. 543 accepts any Enterobacteriaceae), given a manifest with a lineage_taxids column. Needs --species_id_manifest.

species_id_manifest.description: CSV (accession,...,taxid,species_taxid,species_name) mapping reference genome accessions to NCBI taxonomy. Required when any sample has an expected_taxid, since sylph's own output carries no taxonomy; also gives readable species names in the output.

project_alignment_refs.description: Optional CSV of project_id,reference: one reference genome per project, for isolates without their own samplesheet reference.
project_alignment_refs.help_text: For projects with one organism and a stable reference (e.g. SARS-CoV-2 Wuhan-Hu-1, M. tuberculosis H37Rv). The reference is an NCBI assembly accession (GCF_/GCA_..., fetched and cached) or a path to a local FASTA, like the samplesheet's reference column. Priority: the sample's own reference, then its project's, then the species-ID top hit. A project reference applies whatever the species check says. One row per project; relative paths are resolved from the launch directory.

skip_reference_genome_fetch.description: Skip fetching reference genome accessions from NCBI. Off by default since planned deployment environments have network access; a fetch failure retries then degrades gracefully (see conf/modules.config). Local FASTA paths in the samplesheet's reference column are used either way. Offline test profiles set this to true.

reference_genome_cache_dir.description: Directory to cache fetched reference genomes in, keyed by accession (reused across runs). Defaults to a reference_genome_cache directory under the launch directory; override to a shared, persistent location. Only used unless --skip_reference_genome_fetch is set.

skip_assembly.description: Skip draft genome assembly + assembly QC. Off by default (i.e. this stage runs) for pure-culture shotgun libraries; assembly itself needs no external database. Offline test profiles (test/test_full) explicitly set this to true, since the tiny/ultra-shallow fixtures don't assemble meaningfully.

checkm2_db.description: CheckM2 DIAMOND database (assembly completeness + contamination). Optional external download - when unset, those columns are reported as NA and only QUAST contiguity metrics are produced.

busco_db.description: Directory of pre-downloaded BUSCO lineage datasets (it holds a lineages/ subdirectory). Optional - BUSCO only runs when this is set. May hold only some lineages: a lineage that is not there falls back to --busco_default_lineage, which must be. Prefetch a public health subset with bin/fetch_busco_lineages.py.

busco_default_lineage.description: BUSCO lineage for samples with no busco_lineage in the samplesheet and a species (or genus) with no row in assets/busco_lineages.tsv.

skip_alignment_qc.description: Skip alignment-based QC (minimap2 + riker). On by default: each isolate with a reference genome has its reads aligned to it and coverage, alignment-rate and insert-size metrics collected.

cleanup_workdir.description: Delete the work directory when the run finishes successfully (Nextflow's cleanup option). Disables -resume for that run; a failed run keeps its work directory.

skip_speccheck.description: Skip species-specific QC thresholds (speccheck, including QualiBact thresholds) for assembled isolates.

speccheck_criteria.description: Optional custom speccheck criteria CSV. By default speccheck uses its bundled criteria (QualiBact species thresholds plus generic rules).

default_genome_size.description: Backstop genome-size hint (bp) passed as --gsize to the assemblers when a sample has no samplesheet genome_size, no reference genome, and no assets/genome_sizes.tsv taxid entry. A ballpark is sufficient - assembly quality is insensitive to this within ~2x.
